items.title: Jannik Sinner: "The body is the only opponent you can never beat"
items.summary: The Italian tennis star who once described himself as "programmed" has had to reprogramme himself and change the shape of his existence. "I’d erase what I felt the day I left home."
items.content:
The hoodie is still there, as is the loose-limbed walk. Four years ago, he said that away from the court, "the noise switches off—it simply stops existing."

This summer, the noise came from within: his right knee said no. No Canada, no Cincinnati, no New York, no Asia, no ATP Finals in Turin.

His last Grand Slam title came on 12 July, on the grass at Wimbledon, where he won his second consecutive title at the Championships, beating Alexander Zverev in the final. He played 47 matches and lost just three. He beat all the top players, from Carlos Alcaraz and Frances Tiafoe to Daniil Medvedev and Rafael Jódar.

Then came silence, broken only by a few social media clips and a handful of words—always the same: I’m not ready. And finally: See you in 2027.

Jannik Sinner is forced to surrender his throne, but this is no abdication. We should see him back on the court for the Six Kings Slam in Riyadh. In the meantime, he has entered the One Point Slam, scheduled for January 13 during the Australian Open opening week.

Even without his crown, he is hardly at risk of becoming invisible. Until the end of December, every tournament will feature an extra player—the one who isn’t there.We will find Jannik in the questions asked at press conferences, in predictions, in a rankings table that will move on without him, and even in other players’ victories, which will come with a small footnote: Sinner was missing.

An absence has this peculiar trait: it doesn't fade; it grows. The young man who once described himself as "programmed" has had to reprogram himself. And change the shape of his existence, no longer confined to a rectangle.

The world number one who used to measure life in 23.77 by 10.97 meters has discovered there are other ways of measuring it.

But he hasn't changed his mind about which one matters to him.

This interview was a long match that began in August and ended in October, when he announced his decision to take a break.

What remains of a summer spent watching tennis far away from the net?

"I didn't do anything unusual. If the question is what new things I discovered during this time away from the tournaments, the answer is: nothing, but I wasn’t bored. I went to Monza to watch Formula 1 and to Milan for the Gucci fashion show; I played a little more on PlayStation; and I started reading a 600-page book, I Kill by Giorgio Faletti.

I was never idle, nor did I turn my back on tennis because it had hurt me. Quite the opposite: I’ve always worked hard—both in the gym and on court, and with the physiotherapists. Patience is the right word for this period. The body is the only opponent you can never beat. When it tells you to stop, you have to accept it and follow the specialists' advice."

But isn't this kind of tennis too hard on the body? An ankle gives way, a kneecap dislocates, a wrist can no longer withstand thousands of accelerations, a hip wears down from all the twisting. These days, there isn't a tournament without withdrawals.

"Injuries are part of sport. You have to be sensible and understand how much to play and when you need a long-term vision: it's not just about today.

You plant the seeds now, but the harvest takes time. And it's always the work you put in, the preparation, that makes the difference, not luck. Luck helps you win a point, not a match."

In July, 16-year-old Russian player Kristina Liutova won the WTA 250 in Memphis after coming through qualifying. Some people warn of an ogre that devours childhood.

"I don't make the rules, but why deprive teenagers of a great story to tell? They’ve experienced intense emotion, they’ve fought, they’ve worked hard.

There comes an age when sport gives you a voice and allows you to be heard, It becomes a way of understanding who you are and growing up. You can't yet be an adult in society; in so many other fields, you're told you're not old enough.

Sport, on the other hand, gives you opportunities without judging you or asking to see your ID. Look at Lamine Yamal's season:he became a World champion with Spain at 19. Why be afraid that too much youth will cause problems? What if, instead, it opened up new horizons and helped bring out qualities that no one has seen before? Let the kids play.

Kimi Antonelli made his debut before he even had a driving licence. On that note, I've finally managed to get my motorbike licence.

If someone earns their success, I don’t see a problem.Just as Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have every right to be on the pitch, even though they are no longer teenagers, not to mention Djokovic."

"Everything. How to relate to other people, the people around us, how to handle certain situations. We compete in different sports, he's 20, I'm 25, but we talk things through a lot. People ask me: would you trade a Slam for a Formula One race win? Come on, there's no point answering. It's never going to happen."

If you could meet the Jannik of 10 years ago, what would you tell him?

"What I’ve learned: talent without work is nothing. You have to make choices, weigh up their consequences and pursue your goal. I’d tell him to make the most of those moments.

I have no regrets; I wouldn't advise him to take a different path, but I would tell him to choose carefully the people he surrounds himself with. I don't regret anything: my family has always been there, and I've always been able to count on a dad who's also a good cook."

And what about a mother who is reluctant to watch your matches?

"She has improved a lot: she no longer leaves during my matches. Her refusal to sit in the Royal Box at Wimbledon is because she doesn't want to be watched and scrutinised by the cameras when I’m playing. She has a point: she doesn't like the tension, although she's now able to stay calmer."

What does tennis tell us about ourselves, better or differently than other sports? Why does it feel so contemporary?

"I don't know why—you’d have to ask the people who watch it, not the ones who play it. Maybe it brings differences to light and gives them value. Rivalry stems from difference. You win and you lose, and everyone finds their own reason to identify with someone who is like them or someone they’d like to be. That’s what makes it fascinating."

The world wants to see Sinner vs. Alcaraz back on the court. It wants nothing else.

"We aren't all the same; contrasts bring out the best in us. Perhaps I'm seen as the disciplined, stubborn champion, while Carlos is seen as the Mediterranean, flamboyant one.

That's the beauty of it: having someone who pushes you to your limits. Tennis has always thrived on this, from Borg–McEnroe to Sampras–Agassi, and then the two-way rivalry became a three-way one with Federer, Nadal and Djokovic."

Sports heroes are more fashionable than actors. Once upon a time, people dreamt through cinema; today, it's you we see at fashion shows.

"But it's not a competition, and we're not in opposition to each other. American basketball has been interested in fashion for a long time, and its players care about expressing their personalities through their clothes off the court, too.

Nobody is replacing anybody else. I think it's simply a question of different platforms and new faces."

Before you, no one walked onto a tennis court carrying a designer bag. Now people imitate you.

"I feel an affinity with Gucci. I like being a bit different while wearing things that are simple, beautiful and elegant. Just as I love being comfortable, and this brand lets me do that. I'm not a showy person. I don't drink alcohol either: I can't stand the taste. At most, I'll have a little champagne or white wine."

If you could erase one single day from your life and never relive it, which one would you choose?

"It wouldn't be a sporting moment— the defeat in the final against Alcaraz in Paris in 2025 nor the semi-final against Djokovic in Melbourne at the beginning of the year."

"I'd erase what I felt the day I left home. The anguish of saying goodbye to my father in Milan when I was 13 and a half, because our paths were going separate ways and a thread between us was breaking.

We were parting; I was crying because of the pain of separation, and so was he. I could do without that day. It was an overwhelming emotion."

"Maybe it helped me find it, even though I suffered. It made me realise that making a choice means gaining new things while losing others.

There can be pain, but also the awareness that a decision that has cost you so much shouldn't go to waste. You have to do everything you can to make the most of it, without regrets. With commitment, consistency, and hard work."

"The innocence of a winter Sunday spent skiing in the Dolomites with my friends. The feeling of having a lovely day doing something you enjoy. A group of kids who just want to have fun.

I'd also include any moment with my family, and one spent go-karting near Cuneo with racing driver Antonio Giovinazzi and cyclist Giulio Ciccone. I love speed, that's no secret. I need adrenaline; I need to keep boredom at bay."

"I could say the smell of a dessert because I love sweet things."

You are 25. If you could choose what age to be today, would you change anything?

items.title: Il mare che avanza
items.summary: When the sea moves in è un progetto collettivo in cui fotografia e ricerca scientifica s’incontrano per raccontare i cambiamenti che stanno ridisegnando le coste italiane Leggi
items.content:
Come si fotografa il mare? Come si può trasformare qualcosa in continuo movimento in un’immagine capace di raccontarlo e renderlo comprensibile?

È quello che hanno provato a fare sei fotografi – Fabio Barile, Matteo de Mayda, Giorgio Di Noto, Amina Chouairi, Giulia Parlato e Massimo Sordi– con When the sea moves in , che indaga le trasformazioni delle coste italiane e i fenomeni che ne stanno modificando gli equilibri. Il lavoro fa dialogare fotografia e ricerca scientifica, ed è articolato in cinque progetti raccolti in altrettanti libri pubblicati da Witty Books .

Le coste del Mediterraneo sono ecosistemi fragili, minacciati dall’erosione, dai cambiamenti climatici e dalle attività umane. L’innalzamento del livello del mare, gli eventi meteorologici estremi, l’urbanizzazione e il turismo di massa stanno modificando il paesaggio costiero, mettendo a rischio non solo gli equilibri naturali, ma anche la biodiversità, le economie locali e il patrimonio culturale.

“Capire questi cambiamenti, ricostruirne le cause e seguirne l’evoluzione nel tempo è indispensabile per immaginare strategie di tutela e interventi di difesa sostenibili”, spiegano Stefania Rössl e Tommaso Parrillo, curatori del progetto. “Non si tratta solo di fotografare ciò che accade lungo le coste, ma di comprendere attraverso quali strumenti possiamo osservare e interpretare le trasformazioni in atto”.

A partire da questa riflessione ogni fotografo ha indagato un tratto del litorale italiano con il proprio linguaggio, concentrandosi su un aspetto preciso. In Atlas undarum Giulia Parlato osserva il mare attraverso esperimenti condotti in laboratorio, in cui il movimento delle onde è riprodotto in scala per studiare il modo in cui l’acqua interagisce con la costa e modifica la distribuzione dei sedimenti. Parlato fotografa questi ambienti trasformando vasche, materiali e movimenti dell’acqua in immagini che nella loro astrattezza a volte somigliano a dipinti. In altri casi realizza still life che rendono visibili processi che di norma lo sono solo per gli addetti ai lavori, mostrando gli strumenti attraverso cui la ricerca scientifica li studia.

Matteo de Mayda e Amina Chouairi in Lagoonal capriccio esplorano il paesaggio poco conosciuto della laguna di Venezia, in particolare le casse di colmata, isole artificiali nate per sostenere lo sviluppo industriale di Porto Marghera e successivamente abbandonate. Attraverso queste immagini, indagano il cambiamento di questi territori nel corso di più di sessant’anni, raccontando un ambiente fragile e in continua evoluzione, segnato dall’erosione provocata dal traffico navale e dalla progressiva trasformazione dell’ecosistema. Ne emerge una visione inedita della laguna, lontana dall’immaginario turistico di Venezia, che invita a riflettere sul rapporto tra esseri umani e natura.

In Layers di Giorgio Di Noto l’attenzione è di nuovo sui processi e sugli strumenti della ricerca scientifica. Il progetto si concentra sulle tecnologie e sui sistemi di osservazione usati per studiare l’erosione costiera, interpretarne i meccanismi e prevederne l’evoluzione.

Nel testo che apre il suo volume Among , Fabio Barile introduce il paesaggio del Lido di Ostia, al centro della sua ricerca, attraverso la descrizione di una scena apparentemente immobile: una superficie marina quasi piatta, lievemente increspata, una spiaggia sabbiosa e un uomo, il signor Array, seduto con le spalle rivolte al mare. Barile invita a osservare gli effetti del tempo sull’ambiente: le onde che consumano gli scogli, la pioggia che scava la pietra. Le sue immagini si concentrano sul progressivo deterioramento delle architetture balneari e sulla loro lenta trasformazione in sabbia, polvere e sedimento.

La serie Rivoluzione di Massimo Sordi prende invece in esame le falesie di Ortona, in Abruzzo, usandole come punto di osservazione del rapporto tra i fenomeni astronomici – come i movimenti dei corpi celesti e le loro interazioni gravitazionali – e i processi che trasformano la superficie terrestre – come l’erosione marina e il progressivo modellamento delle falesie.

Le immagini di questi lavori non formano una narrazione unica, ma costruiscono un insieme di osservazioni che mettono in relazione luoghi e modalità di conoscenza. Pur affrontando temi complessi e spesso molto tecnici, il progetto ha un intento divulgativo: attraverso la fotografia cerca di tradurre fenomeni scientifici in immagini e racconti accessibili a un pubblico più ampio, stimolando una maggiore consapevolezza delle trasformazioni delle coste del paesaggio mediterraneo.

Internazionale pubblica ogni settimana una pagina di lettere. Ci piacerebbe sapere cosa pensi di questo articolo. Scrivici a: posta@internazionale.it

items.title: Come Cyndi Lauper e i Goonies inventarono gli anni ottanta
items.summary: Una canzone dimenticata e un film che è diventato un oggetto di culto per generazioni diverse Leggi
items.content:
Rimettendo in ordine i dischi ho ripescato un vecchio 45 giri, uno dei primi che avevo comprato con i miei soldi quando ero ragazzino. Su una facciata c’è una canzone pop confezionata per un film di Hollywood; sull’altra un rockabilly un po’ sgangherato intitolato What a thrill , “che sballo”. Le canta entrambe Cyndi Lauper, una delle popstar più famose della metà degli anni ottanta. Il pezzo sul lato A, The Goonies ’r’ good enough , accompagnava I Goonies , un film d’avventura del 1985 diretto da Richard Donner e prodotto da Steven Spielberg. Quella canzone arrivò a lambire la Top 10 statunitense: un risultato discreto per un’artista ormai abituata da almeno due anni ai piani più alti delle classifiche pop. Poi, mentre il film cominciava una sua strana vita carsica da oggetto di culto, la canzone scivolava ai margini del repertorio della sua interprete. Fino a finire quasi dimenticata.

Quelle due canzoni ( Goonies e What a thrill ) sono rimaste incastrate tra She’s so unusual , l’album d’esordio che aveva trasformato Lauper in una star, e True colors , l’album che nel 1986 avrebbe consolidato il suo successo. Nessuna delle due trovò posto in quei dischi. The Goonies ’r’ good enough rimase fuori anche da Twelve deadly Cyns , la sua prima raccolta di successi del 1994. Sarebbe riapparsa in The essential Cyndi Lauper nel 2003, ma ormai era diventata una curiosità laterale: il tema di un film per ragazzi nella carriera di una cantante e autrice di cui perfino un genio indiscusso del novecento come Miles Davis aveva riconosciuto il talento autoriale, incidendo Time after time nel 1985.

Eppure quel piccolo disco dimenticato, con le sue due facciate così diverse, racconta parecchio di Cyndi Lauper. E forse ancora di più degli anni ottanta: anni che le generazioni millennial e post-millennial hanno ricostruito e reinventato riscoprendo e amando anche un film minore come I Goonies .

A metà degli anni ottanta Lauper sembrava fatta apposta per accompagnare una banda di ragazzini un po’ strani, goffi e fuori posto come i Goonies. Anche lei aveva costruito il proprio personaggio di oddball , di eccentrica, mettendo insieme apparentemente a casaccio vestiti da mercatino dell’usato, capelli di tutti i colori, una voce capace di passare dal singhiozzo alla risata, dal cinguettio di un canarino a un registro più alto e pieno, quasi da cantante soul. Perché Cyndi Lauper è sempre stata, a differenza di altre star della sua epoca, anzitutto una cantante. La sua personalità in bilico tra comico e malinconico conservava qualcosa di popolare e sfrontato. E il suo look rattoppato, che univa certe ingenuità hippy a qualche spigolo punk, era pensato per l’estetica frenetica e fluorescente della prima era di Mtv. Nel mondo dei Goonies, dove dei piccoli esclusi diventano eroi di cappa e spada, Cyndi poteva entrare senza neanche cambiarsi. Le bastava essere lei.

La sua canzone, però, che originariamente s’intitolava solo Good enough , non raccontava l’avventura dei Goonies. Era una canzone che parlava di rapporti complicati, aspettative difficili da conciliare con la vita reale. Il ritornello cercava un accordo possibile: quello che va abbastanza bene per te va abbastanza bene anche per me. Insomma: accontentiamoci di quello che abbiamo anche se a volte può sembrare un po’ un casino.

È buffo come certe espressioni tornino a galla nei decenni, ma con significati diversi. Un po’ come i Goonies sono riemersi nell’immaginario collettivo grazie a un bizzarro fenomeno di passaparola intergenerazionale, così l’espressione good enough sarebbe diventata anche una formula tecnologica. Nel 2009 la rivista Wired descriveva la rivoluzione dell’“abbastanza buono”: mp3, chiamate Skype, video compressi e sgranati spesso interrotti dal buffering. Una qualità imperfetta, compensata dalla comodità, dal basso costo e dalla portabilità: “What is good enough for you is good enough for me”, proprio come cantava Cyndi Lauper.

L’arrangiamento, con quelle percussioni riverberate e quei tastieroni così anni ottanta, faceva sembrare tutto più semplice. Quel riff di tastiera iniziale che imita il suono della marimba era un facile escamotage sonoro per farci entrare subito nel contesto esotico di un’avventura un po’ da isola del tesoro. Negli anni ottanta il suono del synth che imitava marimba, vibrafoni o gamelan era un suono “finto” che suggeriva un’idea astratta di oriente misterioso: i Japan e David Sylvian lo usavano con classe e poesia in pezzi come Canton del 1981, gli Alphaville in Big in Japan o Murray Head in One night in Bangkok , entrambi del 1984, lo usavano in modo più furbetto ed esotizzante, proprio come lo usava Cyndi in The Goonies ’r’ good enough .

Il titolo della canzone da Good enough e basta fu allungato in The Goonies ’r’ good enough per legarla indissolubilmente al film, con grande irritazione dell’autrice. È per questo che un brano arrivato al numero dieci negli Stati Uniti sarebbe rimasto a lungo ai margini del suo repertorio: era la stessa Cyndi a detestare la canzone e il costosissimo video promozionale che l’accompagnava.

Il video di The Goonies ’r’ good enough era una piccola follia diretta da Donner e divisa in due puntate. Cyndi Lauper, più clownesca e svitata che mai, deve salvare la stazione di servizio della sua famiglia dalle mire di alcuni creditori. Per riuscirci si infila in un’avventura sotterranea, tra pirati e trappole, incontrando i ragazzi dei Goonies e le Bangles, all’epoca pronte a fare il loro grande salto nel mainstream del pop con pezzi come Manic monday e Walk like an egyptian .

I cattivi hanno le facce e i muscoli dei wrestler: tra le varie attività imprenditoriali di Cyndi Lauper in quel periodo c’era anche quella di manager di alcuni lottatori professionisti. Nel video compare perfino il vero Steven Spielberg: Cyndi gli chiede aiuto gridando mentre si trova su un ponte di corda circondata da pirati ed energumeni, ma neanche lui sa come tirarla fuori dai guai. Cinema, Mtv, musica pop e wrestling convergono in uno stesso spettacolo, con l’esuberanza di un’industria che sta scoprendo quanto pubblico si possa raggiungere mettendo tutto insieme nello stesso frullatore.

Sotto tutto quel chiasso c’è una paura concreta. La famiglia di Cyndi nel video è sgangherata, chiassosa, poco presentabile; sembrano tutti usciti da un film di John Waters se mai John Waters avesse fatto film per famiglie. Cyndi sa bene che chi ha i soldi può portarle via il posto in cui vive e lavora. La paura di restare senza nulla è anche il motore del film dei Goonies, i cui protagonisti cercano un tesoro per impedire che le loro case siano demolite per fare spazio a un campo da golf.

In entrambe le storie l’avventura nasce da una minaccia immobiliare. E in entrambe, per difendere la propria vita bisogna diventare ricchi. L’amicizia dà il coraggio di scendere nelle caverne; per fermare i creditori servono i gioielli del tesoro sepolto. Il denaro compra la possibilità di restare dove si è. Insomma, gli anni ottanta concentrati in poche righe di sinossi.

Alla fine, quegli anni erano proprio questo: la fantasia che un colpo di fortuna possa sottrarti al potere dei soldi degli altri. Riguardando i Goonies e il video di Cyndi Lauper attraverso il filtro della nostalgia, è facile ricordare le biciclette, gli amici e un’infanzia apparentemente libera, lasciando sullo sfondo l’angoscia economica.

I Goonies hanno raggiunto molti millennial attraverso fratelli maggiori, cugini, genitori e videocassette viste fino a consumarle. Il passaggio generazionale era cominciato molto prima di Stranger things , che nel 2016 avrebbe ripreso quella formula di amicizia, pericolo e avventura trasformandola in un nuovo racconto degli anni ottanta. Un nuovo racconto in cui la questione dei soldi rimaneva sullo sfondo ma rimaneva.

In Giovani si diventa , un film del 2014 diretto da Noah Baumbach, parlando di un ragazzo che accosta I Goonies a Quarto potere , un personaggio chiede: “Ma da quando I Goonies è diventato un bel film?”. La battuta coglie lo scarto tra un giudizio sul cinema e l’affetto per un oggetto culturale cresciuto insieme a chi lo guarda e custodito come un prezioso ricordo d’infanzia. Per Brian Eggert, che firma un lungo pezzo sui Goonies su Deep Focus Review, rivederlo è “un esercizio di nostalgia avvolto in altra nostalgia”.

Quando Steven Spielberg, nel 1981, girava I predatori dell’arca perduta faceva già un esercizio di nostalgia: si ricollegava a certi fumetti d’avventura della sua infanzia, così come Umberto Eco in quegli stessi anni rivalutava i fumetti degli anni trenta con cui lui era cresciuto e che, come tutti i bambini della sua generazione, era costretto a leggere di nascosto. Gli anni ottanta sono stati anni di cannibalesco consumo d’infanzie perdute: dal grottesco e opulento Flash Gordon del 1980 diretto da Mike Hodges con la colonna sonora dei Queen, al meraviglioso, terribile mondo parallelo di Watchmen creato nel 1986 dal fumettista Alan Moore, in cui i supereroi degli anni quaranta e cinquanta ormai invecchiati non erano riusciti a cambiare né il mondo né se stessi.

items.title: Kirlian Photography: Building Your Own Equipment
items.summary: Article URL: https://imagesco.com/articles/kirlian/kirlian-photography.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50410359 Points: 55 # Comments: 14
items.content:
What is Kirlian Photography? Kirlian photography is a high voltage, contact print photography.

Kirlian photography is named after Semyon Davidovich Kirlian and his wife Valentina who began their work with high voltage photography in 1939. Kirlian collaborated with his wife for over 30 years developing equipment and studying electro-photography.

Kirlian's work was first made known to the general public in this country by a book published in 1970 by Shelia Ostrander and Lynn Schroeder titled "Psychic discoveries Behind the Iron Curtain". Kirlian work became so well know that the field of high voltage electro-photography is called Kirlian Photography.

Although Kirlian wasn't the first to study electro-photography. The field of electro-photography can be traced back to the late 1700s. At this time Georg Christoph Lictenberg noted the pictures made in dust create by static electricity and electric sparks. Nicola Tesla (1880) photographed many corona discharges using his famous Tesla coil. In the early 1900s, Russian researcher Yakov Narkevich-Todka exhibited electro photographs he had made. A little later, Dr. F.F. Strong of Tufts University Medical School used a Tesla coil to make electro-photographs of his hand.

The process is simple. Sheet film is placed on top of a metal plate, called the discharge or film plate. The object to photograph is placed on top of the film. If the object to be Kirlian photographed is inanimate, such as a coin or leaf, a earth ground is connected to the object. See figure 1 below. High voltage is applied to the plate momentarily to make an exposure. The corona discharge between the object and discharge plate passes through and is recorded onto the film. When the film is developed you have a Kirlian photograph of the object.

The Kirlian process, being a contact print process, doesn't require the use of a camera or lens. However when a transparent electrode is substituted for the discharge plate it is possible to use a standard camera (with a bulb setting) or video camera.

I was first introduced to Kirlian photography, by the book titled "Psychic Discoveries Behind the Iron Curtain" by Shelia Ostrander and Lynn Schroeder in the early 1970's. In it many paranormal claims were made concerning the resulting Kirlian images. For instances, it was said that the Kirlian photograph could foretell illness in plants and animals before physical manifestations of the disease became apparent. I have experimented with Kirlian photography over the years. I have not observed any "paranormal" evidence of this phenomena.

One must keep in mind that most observable Kirlian phenomena does not require any paranormal or bio-plasma field to be explained. For instance, stress or the "act of lying" can easily be detected with a lie detector that relies on measuring the change in a person's galvanic skin resistance. Stress may also be seen in a Kirlian photograph as a change in the corona discharge (aura), however this change is easily explained by the change in a person's skin resistance without the need of evoking any metaphysical properties.

The one observed phenomena and, the most amazing claim (in my opinion) is known as the "phantom leaf" experiment. Here a small portion of a leaf is cut off; the leaf is then photographed using Kirlian photography. In a small percentage of cases the cut portion of the leaf appears in the photograph as a ghostly apparition. The appearance of the cut portion of the leaf, as claimed by the Soviet researchers is proof of an ethereal bio-plasma body.

Although a few Kirlian researchers have claimed to duplicate the phantom leaf experiment in their own labs, the most reported successful results (phantom leaf photographs) are from Soviet researchers. The exact experimental parameters (voltage, frequency, etc) needed to obtain phantom leafs are either not available or didn't work for me.

There are Kirlian devices being sold on the internet today. To sell their devices the corona discharge in the resulting kirlian photograph is claimed to be paranormal or hold information that can be decrypted by the company's Kirlian researchers. All my research to date shows the corona discharge can be explained by employing known physical laws, like changes in subjects skin resistance (due to factors like; stress-lying, illness, fatigue, alcohol consumption, etc) without the necessity of invoking paranormal (bio-plasma) factors. Some other variable factors influencing the resulting Kirlian picture including the object's pressure against film, air humidity, air pressure, voltage, frequency, and exposure time.

This company also sells Kirlian devices and components, but we do not make any "paranormal" claims to try to sell our devices. Our devices are sold to make brilliant Kirlian photographs. If one wants to do research with our devices that fine also. Just know we make no claim that any interpretation of the corona discharge is due to anything other than standard variable physical parameters as outlined previously.

The next page we will begin the construction of a simple manual kirlian device. This device uses a battery power supply, high voltage ignition coild, copper clad board and a handful of components.

The Kirlian device we are building uses a HV transformer. It is battery powered, but don't let that lull you into a false sense of safety. The Kirlian device generates pulses of high voltage that can provide a nasty shock. Still an advantage of being battery powered is portability.

In addition we will build a transparent electrode that allows one to use a standard camera (with bulb setting) to capture Kirlian images.

The schematic is shown in Figure 2 . A completed circuit can be seen below the schematic. This is a simple manual device. It uses very few components. You would be hard pressed to find a simpler device that works as well. The prototype is built on a single piece of wood measuring *" x 10" x �" thick (see photo). The batteries B1 and B2 are 67.5-volt photo (instrument) batteries wired in series to produce 135 volts.

If the photo batteries are not available you may want to try wiring 10 or more 9-volt batteries in series. The discharge will not be as intense, but it will work. Another option is to take the output from a 120V/24V step down transformer connected to a voltage quadrupler. With the 24V (AC) output wired to a voltage multiplier (4x), the unit should produce about 100 volts that can be used for the power supply for this Kirlian device.

The capacitors C1-C4 are wired in parallel as shown in Figure 2.

The transformer T1 is a high voltage auto-transformer. Auto as in self-inductive, not auto, like automobile. The T1 transformer has three wires coming out of it: two enamel wires and one green insulated wire from the center. The green insulated wire is the high voltage wire that connects to the discharge plate. The two enamel wires are the primary wires that are connected to switch SW1. There is no polarity with the enamel wires. So it doesn't matter which enamel wire is connected to the switch, and which is connected to the capacitors. Either way the circuit will function properly.

The toggle switch SW1 is a single pole double throw "momentary" contact. The switch has solder wires on the bottom, see Figure 3. This particular switch doesn't lock or stay in the opposite position. A built in spring immediately brings the switch back to its original position. To operate the device, toggle the switch on and off. When the switch is in the "on" position, it closes a current path to the HV transformer and capacitor bank.

The switch is important and must be wired correctly to obtain maximum benefit. Looking at the schematic shows how the switch appears in its resting state. In the resting state the batteries are disconnected from the circuit. This preserves the life of the batteries. Also the discharge path from the capacitors is closed. This prevents a potential shock hazard from being stored in the capacitors, to be unleashed on an unsuspecting experimenter.

To mount the switch to the board a metal battery clip (9-volt) is used, see parts list. The clip is bent to make a U shape as shown in Figure 3. The center hole in the clip is enlarged to fit the switch SW1. A hole is drilled in each ear of the clip to secure it to the board with two wood screws. The switch is secured to the clip, and then the assembly is secured to the board.

Below is an example of a photograph taken with the Kirlian device.

The exposure (or discharge) plate is made from 4" x 6" single sided copper clad board. The high voltage output wire (green) from transformer T1 is soldered to the corner of the copper clad board. The copper side of the board is placed face up and glued to the wood board.

After the glue dries, the discharge plate is covered with a thin plastic sheet approximately .005 inch thick. The plastic should extend at least 1" past the discharge plate on all sides. The sheet is secured in place by taping or gluing it down.

The thickness of the plastic sheet isn't critical. Anything around this thickness that will prevent the object from making direct contact with the discharge plate. Sheets are available from many art and drafting supply stores. The plastic sheet may be transparent or opaque, it doesn't matter.

items.title: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
items.summary: Saudi Arabia, which leads a coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, has not commented.
items.content:
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say at least 33 people, including women and children, have been killed in air strikes by Saudi Arabia.

There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.

The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.

The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.

Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Saturday. It added that 39 people had been injured.

The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.

The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.

A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plane landing there.

The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.

Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.

On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.

The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.

The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.

Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.

The Saudi Ministry of Energy later said the Aramco tower had been hit by falling shrapnel in what it said was an attempted attack.

The state-owned oil company's building suffered minor damage.

A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

items.title: ISponsorBlockTV: SponsorBlock client for all YouTube TV clients
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.com/dmunozv04/isponsorblocktv Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50410249 Points: 61 # Comments: 17
items.content:
iSponsorBlockTV is a self-hosted application that connects to your YouTube TV app (see compatibility below) and automatically skips segments (like Sponsors or intros) in YouTube videos using the SponsorBlock API. It can also auto mute and press the "Skip Ad" button the moment it becomes available on YouTube ads.

YouTube appers to have changed the screen ID code format and is in the process of revoking all existing codes. This means that you'll have to pair your device again. You can find information on how to do that in the wiki.

Open an issue/pull request if you have tested a device that isn't listed here.

*Ad muting won't work when using AirPlay to send the audio to another speaker.

** Shorts aren't fully supported due to limitations on YouTube's side. A single short can be seen by either selecting the "Disconnect" option in the warning shown or by long pressing the thumbnail to open the menu and clicking play from there

Run iSponsorBlockTV on a computer that has network access. It doesn't need to be on the same network as the device, only access to youtube.com is required.

Auto discovery will require the computer to be on the same network as the device during setup. The device can also be manually added to iSponsorBlockTV with a YouTube TV code. This code can be found in the settings page of your YouTube TV application.

items.title: Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi
items.summary: Article URL: https://caleb.software/posts/claude-to-pi.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50410107 Points: 406 # Comments: 254
items.content:
I’ve been a longtime Claude Code user, ever since it became available in the Claude Pro subscription plan over a year ago. I remember the first time I used it, feeling giddy as it spat out messy Python code for whatever random weekend project I was working on, all from a single prompt. I’m certain that in a few years we’ll all look back at its release as one of the major drivers of this new era of software development we’re in.

Despite this, due to an accumulation of many small frustrations, I’ve finally decided to retire it as my main coding harness and migrate my development setup to use Pi instead.

Someone at Anthropic must’ve caught wind… just a day after making my decision, they announced Claude Code would finally start supporting AGENTS.md files in an effort to get me to stay. Unfortunately, for me it was too little, too late.

In lieu of a proper obituary, I’d like to take this time to say a few words about the things I liked least about Claude Code (and thus what I’m looking forward to avoiding with Pi).

The AGENTS.md thing kind of epitomizes the whole reason I decided to quit using Claude Code. Don’t get me wrong, having a ton of CLAUDE.md files scattered about various GitHub hobby repos is great guerrilla marketing. But it sucks for users to have to deal with copying or symlinking between the two formats.

Like the Luddite I am, I still prefer to review most of the code it churns out before I commit it. I use(d) Claude Code inside VSCode, and it lets you connect the harness to the IDE. This is nice because you can highlight text in a file and have it automatically included in the context when asking questions or requesting changes during a review.

Except you can only have one session “connected” to the IDE at a time. If you open a second tab to start another task while the first one works, it can’t receive the text selection events from the IDE at all. This has been reported at least as far back as December 2025 … and closed as a duplicate of a totally unrelated bug. 1

Of course, you can always use the official Claude Code VSCode GUI extension, which does allow you to have multiple tabs open and load the text selection into the context of each. But this extension has plenty of problems of its own. Half of the built-in slash commands don’t work at all in the GUI. It doesn’t have any support for a custom status line. Subagent output messages are simply layered into the main chat thread in chronological order, which is a mess to read when more than one is running. I could go on and on.

In spite of all of these existing issues, it seems like Anthropic has worked at a feverish pace to pack more features into Claude Code without much care for quality or stability. Dynamic workflows , agent teams , ultrareviews – all great ways to help enterprise customers burn ever more tokens each day, but not really anything I want or need.

Alongside all of these feature releases, they always seem to be fiddling with things in ways that mess up my personal setup. At the time of writing, there have been 244 releases to Claude Code this year; over 3/4 of these changed the system prompt or tool descriptions, which can substantially change how the LLM performs (especially when these new instructions contradict user prompts or repo conventions).

And what are all those changes for? Despite chopping 80% of the system prompt , Claude Code still has way more overhead than Pi for seemingly no benefit. The default Bash tool’s description is almost 3,000 tokens, most of which is random stuff about using git and opening PRs on GitHub. 2 The models already know how to do this without detailed instructions, by the way. 3

This post has been a lot of hating. I’m sorry! That’s not my usual style, and I do think Anthropic has made a really cool piece of software here. I’m also not under any delusion that I would’ve done a better job if I were the one in charge of running Claude Code from the beginning. LLM coding harnesses are a very new space and being one of the first to innovate in a field is a really hard task. Later tools like Pi have the benefit of hindsight to see what works and what doesn’t, what’s a core feature and what can be cut.

Ultimately, CC feels like a product without a strong vision or direction. It’s as if a bunch of excited engineers and PMs are rapidly tacking on whatever features suit their workflow… but without consideration for how this might make things worse for other users. It seems like there isn’t someone high-up whose job is strictly to say “no” to these requests, which is incredibly important when it comes to product engineering. So, for now, I’m leaving.

I’m excited to lean more into Pi. The first few days required some finagling, but since then it’s been smooth sailing. I’m enjoying the stability, minimalist approach, and the extreme level of customizability. I’ve already written a couple of extensions to support my use cases, which I’m hoping to share soon after I’ve cleaned them up a bit. If you’re also feeling these frustrations, I’d highly encourage giving an open source harness a try!

It’s not like there’s some huge technical roadblock to this either. After installing Pi, I wrote an extension to handle this very functionality across multiple open tabs in like 20 minutes. (return)

Bonus points for the fact that it instructs the model to use cat which (prior to widespread rollout of auto mode) would always trip the manual review rules regardless of existing git command allowlists. (return)

If you assume 1 million DAU and 100M requests per day, trimming 1,000 tokens off of this could literally save millions of dollars in inference costs per year. Surely that’s worth some engineer’s time?? (return)

I love hearing people's thoughts, so please don't hesitate to shoot me an email at calebdotsoftware@gmail.com . If you'd like to get updates whenever I publish a new post, you can subscribe over email or with RSS .

If you want to comment or read the public discussion about this post, I've shared it on the following sites: Twitter , Mastodon , Bluesky

items.title: Samsung Secrets: i Samsung AI TV si trasformano in una console di ultima generazione, serve solo un controller
items.summary: Il Gaming Hub di Samsung nasconde un vero PC da gaming all'interno del televisore. Ecco cosa serve per giocare in 4K a 60 fps (e oltre) direttamente dal cloud ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Quando si pensa di acquistare una nuova console da gioco o un PC per il gaming in 4K, ci sono sempre più ostacoli: hardware introvabile e prezzi fuori controllo. Eppure, se in salotto c’è un televisore Samsung AI TV, quella “console” è già pronta all'uso e non ha bisogno di alcuna “scatola" aggiuntiva posizionata sotto lo schermo. Si chiama Samsung Gaming Hub ed è uno degli elementi più potenti — e spesso meno esplorati — della piattaforma Smart TV Tizen. Non è una semplice raccolta di app, ma un ambiente che trasforma il TV in una stazione da gioco di alto livello, azzerando la necessità di acquistare hardware dedicato.

Il principio alla base del Gaming Hub è semplice: l'elaborazione grafica non avviene sul televisore, ma su server remoti ad altissime prestazioni. Il TV riceve un flusso video a bassissima latenza e invia i comandi impartiti dal controller.

A differenza di qualche anno fa, la maturità delle piattaforme di cloud gaming di oggi garantisce una qualità sovrapponibile a quella di una macchina fisica di altissimo livello , e i Samsung AI TV supportano i migliori servizi oggi disponibili per qualità e titoli disponibili:

Dal Gaming Hub puoi sfogliare direttamente il catalogo aggregato dei titoli disponibili, ricevere raccomandazione dei giochi che ti possono interessare, con indicazione chiara dei servizi di cloud gaming in cui li puoi trovare. Basta selezionare il gioco, la piattaforma e sei pronto a iniziare.

Accedere a centinaia di titoli con il Gaming Hub è più semplice di quello che credi: basta collegare un controller. Il Gaming Hub abbatte qualsiasi barriera perché non richiede un gamepad proprietario : Samsung AI TV supportano infatti i principali controller per console e Bluetooth: c’è la compatibilità nativa via Bluetooth o USB via cavo per i controller Xbox, Xbox Elite, PlayStation DualSense e DualShock 4, Amazon Luna.

Come si collega? Dalla schermata principale del Gaming Hub, basta selezionare l'icona del controller per avviare la ricerca Bluetooth ed effettuare l'abbinamento in pochi secondi. Collegando un cavo USB a una porta del TV o del box One Connect, il riconoscimento è immediato e plug-and-play.

E se sei un amante dei giochi in prima persona e non ami il controller da gioco non c’è nessun problema. Puoi anche collegare mouse e tastiera , sia via Bluetooth che tramite le porte USB, e giocare esattamente come da PC. E siccome anche l’audio è importante, con i Samsung AI TV puoi collegare direttamente anche cuffie e auricolari Bluetooth, con gestione dell'audio a 360° e modalità a bassa latenza.

Se invece possiedi già un PC da gaming rig o una console di ultima generazione (come PS5 o Xbox Series X), il Gaming Hub si trasforma nel centro di controllo per le sorgenti esterne via HDMI 2.1. I Samsung AI TV sono equipaggiati di quattro ingressi HDMI 2.1 completi che offrono accesso a tutte le funzionalità aggiuntive dello standard pensate per il gaming.

Collegando un PC da gaming, i modelli Micro RGB, Neo QLED e OLED Samsung più recenti spingono il refresh rate oltre lo standard dei 120 Hz, raggiungendo perfino i 165 Hz , garantendo la fluidità e l’input lag tipici dei monitor da eSports. Grazie al supporto nativo per VRR (Variable Refresh Rate), AMD FreeSync Premium Pro e, sulla gamma OLED, alla compatibilità NVIDIA G-Sync, lo schermo del TV adatta in tempo reale la sua frequenza ai framerate del PC o della console, azzerando tearing e micro-scatti per una schermata di gioco sempre incredibilmente fluida.

Grazie alla funzione ALLM (bassa latenza automatica), i Samsung AI TV riconoscono automaticamente la console o il PC e impostano automaticamente la modalità gioco. Grazie all’IA, il TV riconosce il tipo di gioco e ottimizza automaticamente l’immagine per garantire la resa migliore in base al genere. Premendo l'apposito tasto sul telecomando si richiama poi la Game Bar, un menù dedicato che consente di visualizzare in tempo reale il frame e di accedere rapidamente a tutte le funzioni di gioco. Tra le ultime novità troviamo la funzione MiniMap Auto Detect che sfrutta l’intelligenza artificiale per riconoscere la mini mappa di gioco e la ingrandisce in un riquadro dedicato. Il Virtual Aim Point sovrappone invece un mirino virtuale su schermo per aiutarti ad ottenere maggiore precisione negli sparatutto in prima persona.

items.title: The Trump coalition is shattered - what will Republicans do now?
items.summary: Republicans can stick with Trumpism or chart a new path, writes BBC Washington correspondent Daniel Bush.
items.content:
Republicans are in soul-searching mode after the coalition that powered Donald Trump to three straight presidential nominations imploded in spectacular fashion in the 2026 midterms.

The stunning election defeat immediately raised questions about the party's future post-Trump.

But there are no easy answers as Republicans face the choice of doubling down on Trumpism or trying to chart a new path forward in his final years in office.

The depth of the problem was captured by outgoing Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, who called the midterms "close to an extinction-level event for Republicans".

Others struck a more optimistic tone. Vice-President JD Vance, who blamed the midterm results on public anger over the war with Iran, argued the party could turn things around. Nevertheless Vance acknowledged the fallout will be messy.

"There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why," Vance said.

The wide range of reactions on the right highlights deep fault lines in the party that formed around Trump's improbable rise to the presidency in 2016 and never really went away.

It's too early to tell which faction will win. But while Republicans are still licking their wounds, the intraparty battle Vance predicted is already under way.

The party must decide whether it will be "centred on one figure, one guy, or on a wider set of ideas like conservatism that can win outside the deepest red places," Rina Shah, a Republican strategist, told the BBC.

Critics on the right - the "Never Trumpers" who opposed his first White House campaign - are pushing for a return to the Republican Party's pre-Trump roots, citing the historic losses around the country on election night.

But simply turning back the clock on Trump will be extremely difficult if not impossible to do.

The party has been wholly transformed during Trump's decade-long reign. Most Republicans have shifted to the right on domestic issues like immigration, and rejected the interventionist foreign policy of the George W Bush era that led to the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.

In Congress, the more moderate establishment wing of the party that disliked Trump from the start has almost entirely disappeared, replaced by conservative Trump backers who echo his nativism and populist rhetoric.

That trend continued this year, as old-guard Republicans like John Cornyn in Texas and Maine's Susan Collins, both of whom clashed with Trump over the years, were voted out of office.

Three days after the election Trump appointed Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff , replacing Susie Wiles.

The move signalled Trump has no plans to moderate his policies or message in his remaining years in office. Miller, who had been serving as the president's chief domestic policy adviser, is a longtime Trump aide known for his hardline immigration policies.

One of the architects of the Make America Great Again (Maga) movement, Steve Bannon, predicted a "civil war" in the party after the midterms.

Afterwards, he blamed the Republicans' defeat on the economy and "foreign wars". "I don't think we implemented the Maga programme," he said, calling on Trump to double down on mass deportations.

But other Republican strategists said the midterms were a wake up call for Make America Great Again (Maga) loyalists who want Trump's political movement to outlast his presidency.

"There's still plenty of Maga voters out there who have supported Donald Trump through thick and thin," said Whit Ayres, a Republican strategist.

"But there is also a significant portion of the Republican Party that's non-Maga, and that's a majority now."

The party lost control of the House and Senate, as well as governorships and state legislatures in red states like Texas and Kansas where Democrats had been shut out of power for decades - and where Trump won by double digits when he was on the ballot.

The stunning upsets underscored the fickle nature of political coalitions.

Trump expanded the Republican base in 2024, increasing support with Latinos and younger voters among other key groups. Republicans hailed the gains as a sign of future strength for the party.

Just two years later, the party lost ground with nearly every critical voting bloc. According to a New York Times analysis of voter data, Latino support for Democratic candidates increased by 29 percentage points from 2024-26. Support from young voters 18-29 years old increased by 33 points.

The swings reflected polling ahead of the midterms that found widespread disapproval with Trump's handling of the economy, immigration and the war with Iran.

Democrats also capitalised on a public perception that the Trump family and administration is rife with self-dealing and corruption. The president's focus on the White House ballroom and other Washington construction projects also contributed to a sense among voters that he was more focused on his legacy than addressing affordability issues.

It's a sentiment shared by Benjamin Shrader, the leader of the Young Republicans in Austin, who was still shell-shocked when he spoke to the BBC in Texas the morning after his party was almost wiped out in the state by a Democratic "blue tsunami".

Shrader said Trump was still a "force of nature" when asked to reflect on how the president had used his first public appearance after the results to show off the White House ballroom project.

He hesitated before adding: "I would focus on issues that are not ballrooms, that are not renaming things. I would focus on what matters."

The evidence in the immediate aftermath of the midterms suggests that Republicans could benefit by distancing themselves from Trump ahead of 2028.

Vance tried to thread the needle with his midterm assessment blaming the Iran war and calling for a return to "America First." It was a nuanced critique that broke with Trump on an unpopular war, but embraced a broader political brand that remains popular with the Maga base.

Trump's next moves on Iran will be watched closely by the party for their 2028 implications. An escalation would risk fuelling the concerns voiced by Vance and other "America First" proponents.

In his postmortem statement on X, Vance also echoed the growing calls on the right to reexamine US support for Israel. But he also signalled an openness to making some immigration enforcement changes. That clashes with Miller, a Vance ally who has speared the administration's second-term immigration agenda.

Party strategists said the midterm drubbing complicated Vance's path to the nomination.

"Before this midterm, JD Vance was the odds-on favourite to win the Republican nomination in 2028. After this midterm, the nomination battle is completely wide open," Ayres said.

Potential Trump successors have some time to consider their options, but they'll have to make up their minds relatively soon. Any 2028 presidential hopefuls will face pressure to announce White House bids in the next few months. Some could launch campaigns before the end of the year.

Vance's election analysis was widely interpreted as an unofficial signal of his plans to run. It will likely be a crowded primary field.

Other rumoured White House contenders include Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, Florida Governor DeSantis, former US ambassador to the United Nations Nikki Haley and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie, to name a few.

In the next election cycle, Republican presidential and congressional candidates alike will have tough decisions to make on key issues of the day, from US support for Israel to tariffs to the AI boom.

Trump's power may be diminished as he enters the final two years of his second term, but he'll still have the loudest voice in the party over the next two years. It's unclear whether he will get deeply involved in the process or take a hands-off approach.

Trump has praised Vance and Rubio at different times, but typically deflects questions about who he'd like to see succeed him.

His endorsement will loom as the biggest wildcard in the 2028 Republican primary race.

"It remains to be seen who will jump into that race," Ayres said.

"But I think it's going to be a lot larger and more diverse than we anticipated before the midterm election."

Follow the twists and turns of Trump's second term with North America correspondent Anthony Zurcher's US Politics Unspun newsletter. Readers in the UK can sign up here . Those outside the UK can sign up here .

Four things we learned this week about 2028 White House race

items.title: Germans wrestle with what to do with Hitler's destroyed Eagle's Nest retreat
items.summary: While some believe the site should be partially or completely rebuilt, others want it abandoned and all memory of its Nazi past forgotten.
items.content:
Perched on a ridge high up in the spectacular scenery of the German Alps lie the burned-out ruins of a mountain house called The Eagle's Nest, which is now at the heart of an intense debate about Germany's Nazi past.

Known in German as Kehlsteinhaus, the retreat was built by the Nazis in 1938, and frequented by Adolf Hitler and other high-ranking Nazis and their guests. After World War Two it was classified as a historical monument recalling the Nazi era.

Last month it was gutted by fire in a suspected arson attack, and some believe it should be completely destroyed, the site returned to nature and all memory of its Nazi past forgotten.

But others want it either partially or completely rebuilt, wary of the risk of turning it into a site for Neo-Nazi pilgrimage at a time when Germany is witnessing the resurgence of the far-right.

Germany has an "everlasting responsibility to communicate, to deal with our Nazi past", said Isabel Heinemann, professor of contemporary history at Munich's Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität (LMU).

But rebuilding the site completely, she warned, would mean putting "highly ideologised or highly ideological architecture" back in place.

Before it was burned down during the evening of 23 October, the Eagle's Nest had been a popular tourist attraction, owned by the state of Bavaria and operating for many years as a restaurant.

Visitors would take a bus and then ride the original brass and mirror-panelled lift through the mountain to the Kehlsteinhaus to savour the magnificent views above the town of Berchtesgaden.

Once there, they could eat sausages in the beer garden on the Obersalzberg at 1,834m (6,017ft) above sea level, overlooking the Alps.

Unlike Hitler's nearby summer residence, the Berghof, which was bombed in World War Two and demolished in 1952, the Eagle's Nest survived the war.

Tens of thousands of tourists visited each season, providing an important source of income to the region.

In the 1990s, amid concerns that the site did not do enough to confront the crimes of the Nazi past, a museum, the Obersalzberg Documentation Centre, was opened close by.

Around 15 years ago, a photo exhibit was opened in the Kehlsteinhaus about its history.

Although the Eagle's Nest itself was "largely destroyed" by the fire, according to police, the documentation centre survived unscathed.

The authorities have not commented on a possible motive, but a 33-year-old man with a history of mental illness has been detained in a secure psychiatric hospital on suspicion of arson.

Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat

Some feel this is the moment to allow the site to fade into history.

"It's been torched now. It's been destroyed. I think they should just clear away the rubble and leave the mountain as it should be in its natural state," said Prof Sir Richard J. Evans, a specialist in Nazi Germany at the University of Cambridge.

That has happened with "quite a few other Nazi sites", he argued, including the bunker in Berlin where Hitler killed himself: "The bunker was filled in with concrete and a children's playground put on the top of it on the ground."

The Kehlsteinhaus was just "a Nazi vanity project" since romanticised by the name Eagle's Nest, he said.

But Bavaria's authorities take a different view about the site's future.

Both the state's interior minister, Joachim Herrmann, and its minister for the arts, Markus Blume, have spoken out in favour of rebuilding the Kehlsteinhaus.

Sven Keller, head of the Obersalzberg Documentation Centre, believes it is important not to leave the site in ruins, as that could encourage Neo-Nazi pilgrims, who would be able to hike up there completely undisturbed.

"We have quite some experience at Obersalzberg with what happens if we clear those sites. Hitler's Berghof was demolished in the 1950s, and in our experience, this does not remove such sites from the mental maps of people," he told the BBC's Today programme.

Nor does he believe "a one-on-one reconstruction" of the site is possible, and Blume has made clear on Bavarian radio that "it should not and must not cost the taxpayer anything".

Herrmann said they would look for a sensible solution in consultation with historians, given the historically complex circumstances surrounding the building.

Heinemann, who also heads the Leibniz Institute for Contemporary History, believes full-scale reconstruction should be "out of the question".

"I rather think we can document the state left by the fire and also document the historical remains of the Kehlsteinhaus, and then reconstruct parts in a modern design, to make clear the different layers of time that can be seen in this building," she told the BBC.

Germany and Austria have long struggled to deal with the fraught legacy of buildings and sites connected to the Nazi era.

With the recent rise of the far-right AfD and the Austrian Freedom Party, the debate over Erinnerungskultur (Culture of Remembrance) has taken on a new urgency.

A row broke out recently in Germany when AfD and conservative CDU councillors in a town in Saxony decided to ban "stumbling stones" memorials - embedded small brass plaques in the streets - to victims of the Nazis.

In Austria over the summer, a police station was opened in the house where Hitler was born in Braunau am Inn. It followed years of controversy about how the house should be used.

The Austrian government said the police presence would help prevent neo-Nazi pilgrims.

But others had wanted the house to become a centre of responsibility, actively confronting the Nazi past.

As one resident of Braunau am Inn told me, it was a delicate balance between how much to remember and how much to forget.

items.title: Miller, il bullo del presidente dall’attivismo alla Casa Bianca: “La moglie dietro la nomina”
items.summary: Kate, nota podcaster conservatrice ha mobilitato i vertici Maga affinché appoggiassero l’incarico a chief of staff
items.content:
WASHINGTON – Il neonominato Chief of staff della Casa Bianca , Stephen Miller , sa di essere inviso a molti fin dai tempi della scuola. A 17 anni tentò infatti di farsi eleggere nel consiglio studentesco della Santa Monica High School che frequentava, attaccando i bidelli: «Sono l’unico stufo di sentirsi dire di raccogliere le cartacce da chi dovrebbe essere al nostro servizio?». I compagni lo fischiarono, costringendolo a lasciare il palco, accusandolo di razzismo: gli addetti alle pulizie erano tutti afroamericani.

Classe 1985, nato e cresciuto nella liberal Santa Monica , città costiera a ovest di Los Angeles vera roccaforte dem (qui prendono il 78 per cento), il rampollo di una famiglia ebrea californiana benestante e democratica, è stato un conservatore intransigente e razzista fin da giovanissimo. All’università, per dire, dichiarò guerra alle Fraternity latine perché non promuovevano «valori americani».

Nel tempo si è trasformato in uno dei più influenti ideologi di estrema destra Usa: approdato a Washington per lavorare come assistente del falco repubblicano Jeff Sessions, nel 2015 è diventato ghostwriter di Trump : autore dei discorsi più infiammati contro i migranti, sua vera ossessione visto che è un sostenitore della teoria complottista della «Grande sostituzione» , presunto piano delle élite progressiste per favorire l’immigrazione di massa e “sostituire” la popolazione bianca, a scopi elettorali. Dopo la vittoria del 2016, l’allora neoeletto presidente lo portò con sé alla Casa Bianca. Dove Miller divenne l’architetto delle politiche più odiose dell’amministrazione, sussurrando all’orecchio di Trump prima l’idea del Muslim Ban , l’ordine esecutivo del gennaio 2017, che limitava l’ingresso negli Stati Uniti a cittadini di diversi Paesi a maggioranza musulmana, rimasto in vigore fino all’avvento di Joe Biden. Poi, nel 2018, la crudele separazione delle famiglie di clandestini al confine , con i bambini chiusi in gabbie di metallo.

Nel corso del secondo mandato, consigliere alla sicurezza nazionale, è stato l’istigatore della linea dura dell’Ice : fissando personalmente l’obiettivo di 3mila arresti al giorno e 50mila espulsioni al mese. Fino a definire Renée Good e Alex Pretti – i due americani uccisi mentre riprendevano gli abusi della polizia anti-migranti - «terroristi domestici».

Sopravvissuto alle volatili simpatie del presidente, lo scaltro e astuto Miller è oggi considerato il collaboratore più fedele di The Donald. Chiamato a sostituire quella Susie Wiles appena defenestrata, di cui era il malcontento vice, con l’aiutino della moglie Kate, nota podcaster conservatrice che ha mobilitato i vertici Maga affinché caldeggiassero il suo nome con Trump.

La nomina a nuovo capo di gabinetto ne fa uno degli uomini più potenti del governo statunitense. Non solo uomo di fiducia del leader e in quanto capo dello staff, braccio strategico della Casa Bianca. Ma vero custode del presidente, di cui organizza l’agenda, col potere di decidere quali questioni e documenti possono arrivare sulla scrivania dello Studio Ovale. Filtra poi gli accessi all’inquilino del 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue, decidendo chi può fargli visita. E partecipa alla definizione delle strategie politiche : dalla pianificazione legislativa alle priorità del governo. Infine, è colui che negozia col Congresso . Ruolo che preoccupa molti, visto che è solitamente affidato a figure con solide capacità da mediatore: che lui non ha.

Convinto sostenitore di poteri presidenziali pressoché illimitati, considera il Partito Democratico un’organizzazione estremista e sogna una repressione spietata non solo contro l’immigrazione, ma anche contro qualunque oppositore straniero. Per quanto riguarda i giornalisti - scrive The Atlantic - è favorevole all’arresto di quelli che non rivelano le loro fonti nel governo.

«È stato chiamato a fare il consigliere di guerra», dice Roger Stone che fu uno dei primi strateghi di Trump. «Colui che più somiglia allo spietato Roy Cohn» ci dice invece Kai Bird , biografo del feroce procuratore generale maccartista, che negli anni 80 forgiò il giovane Donald insegnandogli le sue tattiche aggressive e spregiudicate.

Nonostante le dichiarazioni post-elettorali in cui Trump parlava di collaborare con la nuova maggioranza al Congresso, la scelta di Miller è un chiaro segnale ai dem : la Casa Bianca non vuole tregue né mediazioni e, per sottolinearlo, ha scelto un bullo, insensibile alle critiche e ai vincoli della morale tradizionale.

Proprio l’opposto di ciò che ha chiesto il Paese votando contro le politiche dell’amministrazione.

items.title: GitHub New pull request overview page in public preview
items.summary: Article URL: https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-05-new-pull-request-overview-page-in-public-preview/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50408931 Points: 150 # Comments: 101
items.content:
On a long pull request, checking what's blocking often means scrolling past dozens of comments and timeline events just to reach the merge box. And once you're there, you still need to work out what to do next. As people need to review more and more pull requests, time spent scrolling adds up. So we've begun to rethink the entire experience, beginning with addressing a familiar challenge: finding what's blocking progress and determining what to do next.

Today, we're introducing the Overview page as an opt-in public preview, with rollout continuing through the weekend. It brings merge status and next available actions to the top of the page in a compact readiness summary. It's the first step toward making pull requests easier to follow as code, conversations, and reviews evolve.

We're starting with the merge box, the place developers go to see whether a pull request can move forward. Rather than just moving it higher, we've also redesigned it to show the same information in less than half the space.

Start with the summary, then follow the detail that matters to your next step (e.g., get to failing checks, see who still needs to approve, or open the relevant comments).

This first preview also introduces more ways to catch up on activity and focus the conversation so you can spend less time finding your place.

You can also mark a draft ready for review or close a pull request from the header, with available actions depending on your permissions.

To join, select the ✨ Try the Overview page button in the header. We're opening this preview early so you can try the new direction on your own pull requests and help shape what comes next. You can use the same menu to return to the classic overview during the preview.

This preview is very much a starting point, not the finished pull request experience. Try it on your next pull request. What is easier to find? Where do you still lose context? What sends you back to the classic overview?

Share your feedback and report issues in the overview preview feedback discussion .

items.content:
There's a cute math puzzle that can be interesting to folks on very different levels:

In middle school, kids learn about exponents, factorials, etc. which expands the range considerably:

Then come the tricks; for example, the number 22 (twenty two) can be seen as a valid use of two 2s, and so on; so we can have:

Getting to 7 is notoriously difficult, but if you allow even more mathematical tools like the Gamma function , it becomes easy:

The more math skill people have, the more numbers they can make. See this thread for some fun concoctions using integrals, repeating fractions and combinatorial operators. One of my favorite examples involves complex numbers:

So the fun doesn't end even after one graduates from university! In fact, this seems to have been a favorite pastime for mathematicians in the 1920s. Until Paul Dirac ruined it for everyone by finding a general solution for every number.

There's just one small wrinkle: it uses three instances of the digit 2, not four. This is easy to amend, however; since 2=\sqrt{2+2} , we can replace any single digit with that and get exactly four:

One may claim this is cheating, but it seems to be in line with the rules of the puzzle! Note that the entity n doesn't actually appear anywhere - it's just a helper to count the number of repeated square roots. For example, another way to express 7 is:

There are exactly four 2s, and this uses only reasonable, elemental math operations to do the calculation. It's clear that any number can be expressed this way; the only challenge is properly drawing all those square roots!

I've read about this story in Graham Farmelo's book The Strangest Man: The Hidden Life of Paul Dirac, Quantum Genius . I'm enjoying this book so far.

items.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
items.summary: Neither PM Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor that of his rival secured a majority in last week's election.
items.content:
Israel's president says he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government.

Isaac Herzog has been holding talks with political parties after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, following last week's election.

Eisenkot will now have 28 days to try to form a new administration, with a potential 14-day extension.

"Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," the former military chief wrote on X.

No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, meaning all governments have been coalitions.

Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.

Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.

Herzog said that, after consulting all parties during the week, he would give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government.

A statement from the president's office said he had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision.

Following consultations with delegations from the incoming Knesset members, Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership and Netanyahu 46, the statement said.

The president has broad discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition and does not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.

The election results had implied three possible options for the formation of a government : a national unity administration involving both Netanyahu and Eisenkot, a right-wing coalition involving Netanyahu and defectors from Eisenkot's bloc, or an Eisenkot-led government supported by the Arab parties.

Eisenkot and every member of his bloc bar one has previously refused to enter government with Arab parties, but there has been speculation that an agreement could be reached.

He could also attempt to reach a deal with ultra-Orthodox parties, but that too would be difficult.

There is precedent for a unity government. In 2020, following three deadlocked elections, Netanyahu and his centrist rival Benny Gantz agreed a power-sharing deal in which the leadership rotated between the two.

During his consultations with the parties, Herzog had said that to prevent another round of elections and to build a stable government, he expected "factions and their representatives to understand that, in the current reality, not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled".

In the period 2019 to 2022, one of the most politically fractured in Israeli politics, there were five separate elections as Netanyahu and his rivals struggled time and again to co-operate.
